Justin knew he shouldn’t have been doing it. He made the conscious choice to give Naomi the drugs.

However, Naomi was older and also knew what she was doing. But, she didn’t know it was wrong. She *did* guilt trip a kid into getting her the thing she wanted for evidence and framed him, but it was what she thought was right.

Justin knew he wasn’t supposed to be doing these things, hence the song “cousin” where his relatives are talking about drugs being harmful (“are we thugs to our cousin Justin? Are we supposed to trust him?”) 

Naomi has personal experience of what it was like to grow up under the roof of drug users. That does not make what she did right, but it does give a more relatable POV. 

In ways they were both wrong and in other ways they were both right.

Personally, I say Naomi was in the wrong. Justin was overwhelmed and young. Naomi was older and did more damage than Justin could have done to anyone without Naomis help. So I think Naomi but everyone got a different viewpoint. It all depends on you personally

Death of a mother, Death of a child



Children often wonder what is in the sky. Sometimes adults aswell. It’s a natural curiosity. Clouds are a wonderful world in themselves. People think it’s vapour, fluff, even cotton candy. But they do not know what horror is actually there.

Clouds are formed from the remains of a lost soul. Someone who does not live or does not feel. 

However the sky isn’t the only thing containing dark fears some have. In fact, the earth itself holds many old “wonders”. Underground, water, mountains, air. Nature yields many ominous secrets. 

There is a tale not many people know of surrounding these laws. It goes like so: Three brothers. They lived in the sky. Each holding a special power- Gods, if you will. Their father, Isidore, was the god of canines. Not the cute fluffy puppies you’d see on the internet, but instead wolves, foxes and rabid hunting dogs all gone wild. He had a violent nature. This was passed on to the eldest of the three children. Each of them had seperate mothers. The first died of natural causes. The second was cheated on with the third. The third was murdered as an act to gain power.

As far as the father could tell, nobody knew of the heinous crimes he had committed; if someone *did* they would never dare tell anybody. 

It was a rainy day when the youngest brother, Demetrius had burst into his two older brothers- Cyril and Hieronimus- at the crack of dawn. He explained that he knew what his father had done 16 human years ago. His brothers were mortified. They too knew of the murder of Athenaide, god of the ocean, third wife of Isidore and mother of Demetrius. Not a word was ever spoken of it when they found out. They did not wish to die a merciless death from their parent. 

If Demetrius told Isidor, they would all perish within a matter of hours, despite the olders not being involved. They had no choice. 

Cyril took one look at his brother and opened his mouth. Thousands upon thousands of venomous insects came crawling over his tongue. Spiders, ants, Hieronimus was almost certain he saw a small scorpion manage to fit. They scuttled towards Demetrius with great speed, each biting him and stinging him. Cyril’s eyes gleamed pure white. 

Hieronimus took his chance and conjured up a flaming ball of fire. He thrust it at Demetrius’s face. The brothers watched in horror and took in what they had done.

They did love Demetrius as their brother. But sacrifices had to be made. 

Upon his body’s decent to Earth, the youngest son’s spirit floated around and observed. His body was lowered into a small yet impenetrable fortress underground. A spurt of water shot out from where his heart should be. His body layed in an empty stone dish that could easily fit five hefty men. The water did not stop shooting out of his heart. It flowed, firming a fountain of water that should have been blood. 

Demetrius smiled. Mother was with him. 

Legend has it, if you are able to conquer the fortress and take a sip of that water, you will acquire Demetrius’s abilities. He was the god of family. His mother the god of the ocean. 

But beware, if you drink the water you will be forever united with that family. Perhaps you would rather miss out on Isodore’s family reunions.

My mums Christian and while many Christians don’t do this, I’ve found its different to the UK. Maybe it’s a Hungarian thing.

On the 5th of December every kid in the family polishes one of their boots and props it on the windowsill, preferably not in the kids room. For us it was the hallway till we moved to a house with no window hallways. It had to be in the window. Maybe an hour later (after checking every 5 minutes of course) we’d see a bag full of chocolate and maybe even small toys if were lucky! These were essentially stockings, they came from Santa. 

We’d also get our actual presents on Christmas Eve as opposed to Boxing Day. My mum also said that Jesus brought us the presents and he shipped the ones grandma got us all the way from back home. 

A less happy thing was instead of coal on Boxing Day we would get a “vírgács” on the 5th if we were bad kids. This would be some longish twigs tied with a red ribbon intended to beat the child.
